ns2:section.sectionText: This is a practical course on field research, whose primary purpose is to provide firsthand experience in gathering data on wild birds for scientific research. This course will focus on avian field research techniques, specifically bird monitoring, bird identification, and bird banding. Students will learn about why monitoring bird populations is important in the context of monitoring changes in the environment. In order to monitor bird populations, individual birds must be detected and identified; we will therefore work on bird identification skills. Students will be also be exposed to the skills necessary for banding birds (given the need to socially distance, we will show the students how to choose an area for nets, how the nets are erected, how birds are extracted from a nest, but there will be limited hand-on experience). This class will meet at University of Illinois Arboretum, except for the first class which will meet on Zoom. To request being added to the waiting list for this course, complete the form at http://go.illinois.edu/NRESwaitinglist.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Restricted to Natural Resrcs & Environ Sci major(s). Restricted to students with Junior or Senior class standing.
